title: QR-Map: A Map-Based Approach to Quantum Circuit Abstraction for Qubit Reuse Optimization
problem: Identifying optimal qubit reuse opportunities in quantum circuits via mid-circuit measurements is NP-hard in the general case; existing frameworks either suffer from exponential search complexity or produce non-optimal results due to non-deterministic heuristics.
motivation: Quantum devices have severely limited qubit counts, so efficient mid-circuit qubit reuse directly determines whether practical algorithms fit on near-term hardware, but current compilation tools cannot guarantee optimality without prohibitive runtime.
method: QR-Map abstracts computational dependencies by extracting and aligning two-qubit gates into a map structure, making dependency detection deterministic and tractable. The framework identifies qubit reuse opportunities by analyzing these aligned gate maps, ensuring qubit savings without introducing excessive idle time. It jointly optimizes gate serialization depth and crosstalk reduction, balancing circuit fidelity with hardware constraints through a deterministic, polynomial-time map-based search.
key_novelty: A map-based circuit abstraction that aligns two-qubit gates to expose qubit reuse dependencies deterministically, replacing exponential DAG search with a structured, optimal qubit-reuse framework.
contributions: QR-Map framework providing deterministic, near-optimal qubit reuse without exponential search.
Average 20% reduction in qubit usage compared to state-of-the-art frameworks.
Average 25% reduction in circuit depth and 22% reduction in SWAP insertions.
A balanced optimization of gate serialization depth and crosstalk reduction.

metrics.accuracy: 20% average qubit reduction, 25% circuit depth reduction, 22% SWAP reduction vs state-of-the-art

limitations: Not discussed; results are based on benchmarks and may not generalize to all circuit topologies or noise models.
primary_theme: Map-based qubit reuse optimization for quantum circuits
